statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress holds at 53 in the elevated band rather than easing further: another hour passed with no verified escalation and Aramco reports no significant structural damage, but satellite analysis now shows substantial impact at two pumping stations and the IEA has cut its 2026 supply outlook by a further 1.4 million barrels a day. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and the advance was broad, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and semiconductor gains spread across ARM, QCOM, INTC and AMD rather than concentrated in one leader. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly eight hours after this horizon's final slot closes, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. Third, the verified political direction remains restraint: Riyadh has paused retaliation at Baghdad's request while reserving its rights, Iraq has removed its Maysan operations commander and closed the Shalamcheh border crossing, no group has claimed the attack, and Gulf states are due to meet Iran in Oman on Monday. No evidence-based danger window is published, because no window inside this horizon contains a tradeable session. Stress at 53 describes an unresolved supply picture and a hawkishly priced policy week; under the fixed mapping Stress does not alter the machine state on its own.
headline: Seventeen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and this hour resolved the damage question in two directions: Aramco reports no significant structural damage to the East-West pipeline, while satellite analysis shows substantial impact at two separate pumping stations and the IEA has cut its 2026 supply outlook by a further 1.4 million barrels a day.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources. The price picture is unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend: the Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%, a curve consistent with a hawkish policy path rather than a growth scare.

Friday's participation was broad rather than narrow. Seven of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, and semiconductor strength was spread across ARM at +4.17%, QCOM at +2.88%, INTC at +2.61% and AMD at +2.49% while NVDA finished essentially flat. Breadth of that kind is a poor precursor to the squeeze-type one-way structure this Tail score is built to detect, and it is the main reason the conditional path into an eventual reopen is scored as gap exposure rather than as trend risk.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and already priced. Friday's inflation print showed headline consumer prices up 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both in line with consensus, with core CPI at 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. Market-implied odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September meeting were priced near 87% after the release, up from about 72% the previous day and roughly 50 to 59% a week earlier. Equities rose anyway, which reporting attributed to the retreat in crude rather than to the inflation data. That meeting carries updated economic projections and a press conference thirty minutes after the decision, a structurally multi-stage sequence that warrants care rather than an automatic block. Those are Wednesday checkpoints and sit outside this twenty-four-hour horizon.

The Gulf supply picture is the live unresolved item, and this hour sharpened it in both directions rather than simply improving it. Saudi Arabia's 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline, which had been moving four to five million barrels a day or roughly four to five percent of global supply while bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut as a precaution while specialist teams secure it and assess its safety; no restart timeline has been published, though a comparable repair in April took about three days. On the reassuring side, the energy ministry's preliminary assessment reports no significant structural damage. Against that, satellite analysis now indicates substantial impact at two separate pumping stations with extensive fire damage at one, the IEA has cut its 2026 global supply outlook by a further 1.4 million barrels a day and no longer expects normal Gulf flows to return this year, and the Red Sea picture has deteriorated: Houthi forces have taken Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the port of Mocha, declaring navigation safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels, so both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb are now impaired. Politically the direction is still restraint. Riyadh has paused retaliation at Baghdad's request while reserving its rights, Iraq has removed the Maysan operations commander and closed the Shalamcheh crossing with Iran, no group has claimed responsibility, and Gulf states are due to meet Iran in Oman on Monday over safe shipping routes through the strait. Crude settled lower on Friday in response to those diplomatic contacts, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81%, and WTI at $100.05, down 2.37%. That mix is why Stress holds at 53 this hour instead of continuing its decay.

The binding constraint on this assessment is structural rather than informational. CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly eight hours after the last slot in this horizon. Every forecast hour therefore describes a market with no tape, in which shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension and holding near session extremes cannot be observed because they cannot occur. Conditional Tail rises from 6 to a ceiling of 12 across the horizon, one point above the previous hour's ceiling to reflect the harder supply reality, and that drift is an accruing reopen-gap premium for unpriced weekend headlines rather than a directional view. The most informative checkpoint inside the horizon is the Sunday Gulf cash session, the only venue that can price the outage before the CME reopen; it is cross-asset context, not NQ price-path evidence. Shared supplementary cross-asset context was fresh this hour but flagged partial, with its calendar section unavailable; its healthy sections were latest-session and delayed by construction, and they only confirmed the independently verified Friday picture above, so they did not move any score.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 14:00 UTC on 11 September to 13:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens inside the U.S. afternoon that followed the 12:30 UTC inflation print, with Tail between 13 and 17 in mixed mode and Stress at 82 decaying steadily as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since settled into a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final sixteen slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell monotonically from 82 to 53 over the twenty-four hours, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, easing from 89 to 85 as the last observed price reference aged.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly eight hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then drifts through 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 53 down to a 50 floor late on Saturday and back up to 56 in the final slot, describing the environment rather than a path: an East-West pipeline outage with no restart date and substantial impact reported at two pumping stations, a Strait of Hormuz effectively shut since March and a Bab el-Mandeb now under Houthi control, an IEA supply outlook cut by a further 1.4 million barrels a day, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, and a 16 September policy decision with projections priced near 87% for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to an 80 floor, remaining inside the high band because the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced; the limitation is the freshness of price, not the breadth of coverage. The named checkpoints are the Sunday Gulf cash session inside this horizon, and beyond it the Sunday evening futures reopen, the Monday Gulf-Iran meeting in Oman and Wednesday's policy decision.
